messages:
maya: quick follow-up from the RBAC split RFC — we need a concrete decision on enforcement boundaries before the next sprint. do we move checks into the query router, keep them at projection time, or try a hybrid?

anita: +1 urgent. main constraints: 99th p latency budget for panels (120ms) and the audit log requirement for enterprise. moving checks earlier helps provenance but might add ~15-30ms per request.

sam: can we quantify that? last perf run (staging) showed query-router auth + cache hit had median +9ms but 95th +27ms on heavy panels.

liam: big caveat: if we enforce too early we need to duplicate model of tenant/role mapping in the router. that increases rollout complexity and edge-case bugs. cache invalidation becomes trickier too.

nora: thought: hybrid approach — coarse-grained pruning at the router (tenant-level and route allowlist) then final object-level enforcement post-projection. reduces attack surface and keeps fine-grained logs where we can attribute.

maya: that maps to two goals: 1) protect SLOs by rejecting obviously forbidden requests earlier, 2) keep auditability and exact denial reasons at projection time. what are tradeoffs for cache hit rates?

anita: early denies drop some cache hits because keys include role set. if we keep cache keyed by tenant+panel+query-shape and apply object-level filter after, hit rate improves. downside: we might fetch extra data only to filter later. cost up ~3-4% in tokens in our sim.

sam: another angle: add a tiny async prefetch/validate path for heavy panels. router responds quickly with "pending-auth" and we stream progressive updates. but that's more UX work in console.

liam: progressive responses will require front-end changes. also complicates rollback. not ideal for a small win.

nora: config sketch:
```
rbac:
  router_enforcement: coarse    # tenant / route allowlist
  projection_enforcement: strict  # object-level checks and audit logs
  cache_key: tenant|panel|query_shape
  canary: 10%
```

maya: that looks good. can we define the rollout canary and metrics? propose: 10% traffic -> measure panel latency p95, auth-fail rates, cache-hit rates, CPU on router nodes. SLA guardrails: if p95 > 140ms or cpu > 75% or auth-fails increase > 0.5% rollback.

anita: include business metrics: failed renders due to auth should be <=0.01% for stable. also log latency breakdown: router_auth_ms, projection_auth_ms, fetch_ms.

sam: +1. can we automate the rollback condition in deploy pipeline?

deploy-bot: canary rollout created: `deploy canary eng-platform/console-rbac-split --percent=10 --watch --rollback-on=metric:p95>140ms,metric:router_cpu>75`

liam: a few action items: 1) infra to add router auth store (read-only snapshot) + consistency checks, 2) add cache key change and sim runs, 3) front-end UX fallback for progressive status (low priority).

maya: i'll file the follow-up tickets and assign reviewers. next steps: implement router read-only store (anita), add perf sim (sam), prepare canary dashboard (nora). aim to start canary in 2 weeks.

nora: leaving a note: ensure audit logs contain original request id and final denial reason so we can trace early rejects vs projection rejects.

maya: thanks all. will post RFC follow-up doc link in #eng-platform when tickets are up. :thumbsup:
